era: PlayStation / PlayStation 2 / Xbox / PSP / Nintendo DS / Xbox 360 / Wii
summary: Acquire, K2, and FromSoftware's ninja stealth-action series, including the PlayStation originals, expanded ports, handheld entries, and later Xbox/Wii experiments.

entries.title: Tenchu: Stealth Assassins
entries.definitive_edition: Western PlayStation release, with Shinobi Gaisen as a presentation supplement

emulation.notes: DuckStation can improve PS1 image quality with PGXP/upscaling while preserving the original release.

primary.why: The Western PlayStation release added two levels, alternating mission layouts, technical improvements, a level editor, and a cheat menu over the original Japanese launch. It is the best main route for English play and fuller gameplay content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the North American PlayStation disc on DuckStation or original hardware; use PGXP/upscaling if emulating, and avoid the censored UK build if you want the uncensored item set.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japan-only re-release presentation with a new opening
secondary.what_to_play: Check Shinobi Gaisen only for its Japan-only presentation differences after playing the Western release.
secondary.why: It reissued the Western-expanded version in Japan with a new opening, but the main mission content overlaps the primary route.

entries.title: Tenchu: Shinobi Hyakusen

emulation.notes: Use PS1 emulation for image cleanup; the game remains a Japan-only challenge expansion.

primary.why: Shinobi Hyakusen is a standalone Japan-only expansion built from one hundred selected user-created levels made with Shinobi Gaisen's level editor. It has no other documented platform route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Japanese PlayStation disc on original hardware or DuckStation; expect non-story challenge levels rather than a new campaign.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or localized release exists.

entries.title: Tenchu 2: Birth of the Stealth Assassins
entries.definitive_edition: Japanese PlayStation release for completeness; North American release for English

emulation.notes: Use DuckStation with PGXP/upscaling for the PS1 release; choose region based on language versus completeness preference.

primary.why: The Japanese PlayStation release came after the North American and European versions and added further graphical/technical improvements plus expanded level-editor objects. It is the most complete technical version, while the North American release remains the best fully English route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Japanese PlayStation release on DuckStation for the most complete technical build; use the North American disc instead if English text and voices matter more than the extra Japanese editor/technical improvements.

secondary.exclusive_content: English localization without the European censorship changes
secondary.what_to_play: Use this version if you want the story in English.
secondary.why: The Japanese release has the technical/editor edge, but the North American release is the cleanest localized route.

emulation.emulator: Original Xbox hardware / xemu if compatible
emulation.notes: Prefer the Xbox release for added content; Insignia can restore online play for supported original-Xbox games.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox rendering, potentially higher via emulator

primary.why: The Xbox port added graphical improvements, two new single-player missions, two multiplayer characters, extra special moves, and online play over the original PS2 release. The PSP port includes Xbox features except multiplayer, so the Xbox version is the most complete high-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Tenchu: Return from Darkness on original Xbox hardware or a compatible Xbox emulator; use Insignia only if you specifically want restored original-Xbox online functionality.

entries.title: Tenchu: Fatal Shadows
entries.definitive_edition: PS2 original plus PSP costume supplement

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 for the main playthrough; PPSSPP only for the PSP costume supplement.

primary.why: Fatal Shadows was built for PS2; the later Japan-only PSP version is optimized for handheld screen size and adds new costumes, but the PS2 version remains the better full-screen/fidelity main route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscale; use the PSP port only for its added costumes.

secondary.exclusive_content: New character costumes in Tenchu Kurenai Portable
secondary.what_to_play: Check the PSP version only for the added costume content.
secondary.why: The PSP port has exclusive costume additions, but lower handheld fidelity than the PS2 original.

entries.title: Tenchu: Time of the Assassins

emulation.notes: Upscale the PSP release and use the European version for official English text.

primary.why: Time of the Assassins was released only for PSP in Japan and Europe, with multiple playable series characters and an expanded mission editor. There is no higher-fidelity console or PC edition documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP version on PPSSPP with internal-resolution upscale; use the European release if you want the official English-language route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or North American release exists.

emulation.notes: Use DS hardware or an emulator with dual-screen layout support; original Wi-Fi item trading is no longer a normal modern route.

primary.why: Dark Secret was developed for Nintendo DS and released only on that platform, with more than 40 missions plus local wireless and Wi-Fi item-trading features. There is no alternate edition documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS hardware or melonDS/DeSmuME; expect discontinued online features to be a preservation caveat.

emulation.notes: Original Xbox 360 hardware is the safest route; check emulator compatibility before committing.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox 360 HD output, potentially higher via emulator

primary.why: Tenchu Z was released only on Xbox 360 and centers on custom player-created ninja characters with Xbox Live four-player co-op. No alternate edition is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware or Xenia if compatibility is acceptable; treat Xbox Live-era online co-op as an availability caveat.

entries.title: Shadow Assault: Tenchu

emulation.notes: Because it was a downloadable Xbox Live Arcade title, entitlement/storefront availability may matter more than emulation.

primary.why: Shadow Assault: Tenchu is an Xbox 360 downloadable spin-off with puzzle/action play and multiplayer, and no alternate platform route is documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox Live Arcade version on Xbox 360 if already owned/downloadable; preservation depends on account and storefront availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster exists; digital storefront availability is the main caveat.

emulation.notes: Use Dolphin with Wii input mapping for the primary route; PPSSPP is acceptable only for the handheld port.

primary.why: Shadow Assassins was developed for Wii first, with Wii Remote/Nunchuk movement and sword-fighting controls. The PSP version is generally the same game but changes controls to fit handheld input and removes motion controls, so Wii is the intended primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Wii version on original hardware or Dolphin with Wii Remote/Nunchuk input; use the PSP version only if portability matters more than intended controls.
